On the documented current configuration—`SecPal/operations` is private on the organization Free plan, where branch-protection requests are rejected—adding this key makes both bulk modes call an unavailable protection endpoint. `known_repositories` feeds the fail-fast loop at lines 333–339, so the nonzero `gh api` result aborts `--apply` and `--apply-review-baseline` at `operations` and leaves the lexically later `secpal.app` repository unsynchronized; `gh help exit-codes` confirms that “If a command fails for any reason, the exit code will be 1.” Keep non-applicable repositories separate from the apply inventory rather than suppressing the error, so bulk synchronization remains fail-closed.

issue.body:
## Goal

Onboard private `SecPal/operations` into the shared repository and canonical work-graph audit sources. This is one bounded repository-registration contract, delivered by existing PR #706.

## Accepted repository role and governance

`SecPal/operations` contains executable delivery-controller functionality as well as private architecture and operational documentation. Its Controller implementation, validation, delivery governance and operational installation have separate existing owners; this registration issue does not implement or install them.

Authenticated GitHub observations on 2026-10-11 establish:

- The organization plan is GitHub Team and `SecPal/operations` remains private.
- Active ruleset `24659985` protects the Operations default branch through required PRs, deletion/non-fast-forward protection and no bypass actors.
- Its independently managed required check is `SecPal operations credentialless validation`, with strict status checking and GitHub Actions app binding `15368`.
- The accepted workflow declares that identity and its real hosted producer has successful evidence on accepted Operations PR #86. This is not an absent-workflow or empty-check repository.

These observations describe existing controls, not a new protection policy or a production-readiness claim. Do not infer required signatures, secret scanning or other controls without their own authenticated evidence. Historical information-only and GitHub Free limitations remain historical context, not current assumptions.

## Scope

- Include `SecPal/operations` in `scripts/secpal_work_graph/audit.py`'s maintained default inventory and update the corresponding inventory tests.
- The canonical audit inventory is exactly `SecPal/.github`, `SecPal/android`, `SecPal/api`, `SecPal/contracts`, `SecPal/deployment`, `SecPal/frontend`, `SecPal/operations` and `SecPal/secpal.app`.
- Consume completed Polyscope repository registration through SecPal/.github PR #720 and evidence-governance adoption through `SecPal/operations#5` / SecPal/operations PR #7; do not redeliver either responsibility.
- Reconcile obsolete onboarding descriptions and assertions in PR #706 against the accepted current role and governance facts. Consume completed GuardGuide retirement #990 / PR #1177; neither retired repository belongs in an active inventory.
- Keep organization membership, canonical audit membership, Polyscope registration and required-check synchronization membership distinct. Preserve the existing shared synchronization inventory and separate Operations ruleset/validation ownership; do not add an obsolete empty Operations entry.
- Preserve the permanent information-security boundary: private Git is not a secret store. No credentials, provider tokens, private keys, production/customer secrets, customer data, cryptographic authority or mutable live infrastructure state may be introduced.

## Existing ownership boundaries

- Existing Operations Controller deliveries, including SecPal/operations#16 / PR #17, SecPal/operations#83 / PR #84 and SecPal/operations#85 / PR #86, retain their implementation, merge-gate and validation responsibilities.
- `SecPal/operations#11` retains the distinct future Managed Operations privileged-execution and authority-boundary gate under `SecPal/operations#10`. Controller source and this registration do not establish acceptance of that gate.
- SecPal/.github#1061 retains central lifecycle-publication enrollment ownership. It is not absorbed into repository/audit registration.
- Preserve the existing native dependency from `SecPal/operations#1` to this issue. Final audit SecPal/.github#676 consumes this issue's completed registration through its native prerequisite.

## Acceptance criteria

- The maintained default audit inventory and exact corresponding tests cover all eight active repositories, including private `SecPal/operations`, and exclude retired GuardGuide identities.
- Shared onboarding descriptions reflect the executable repository and existing workflow-backed, independently managed validation policy without falsely claiming absent or unauthenticated controls.
- Completed Polyscope registration, evidence-governance adoption and retirement work are consumed; their owners and unrelated inventories remain unchanged.
- No obsolete empty Operations required-check synchronization entry, new check/protection requirement, duplicate resolver or Controller responsibility is introduced.
- The repository remains private and no prohibited sensitive material is introduced.
- No GitHub plan upgrade is required without a genuine current unmet capability requirement established under its own accepted owner.
- Existing PR #706 remains the primary delivery, with its signed commits, review evidence and finite lifecycle preserved. Any continuation or recovery must be admitted by maintained current-head authority; this contract grants no review-budget reset or new review request.

## Non-goals

Controller development or installation; application deployment; privileged Operations automation; host/reference-server/cloud operations; lifecycle enrollment; changing rulesets, branch protection, required checks, signatures, secret scanning or repository visibility; reviving retired repositories.

## Delivery

Continue existing PR #706 with `Fixes #705` only through the canonical current-head and finite-review procedure. Preserve historical comments and lifecycle evidence. No replacement PR or automatic Draft transition is authorized by this reconciliation.

issue.body:
## Goal

Complete central delivery-governance capability onboarding for active SecPal delivery repositories, so ordinary Draft and Ready deliveries can select accepted lifecycle and integration authority without ad hoc prerequisite discovery.

## Coordination contract

This is coordination and authenticated final capability-matrix completion only. No implementation PR delivers this Epic. The accepted central registry and maintained verifier/executor remain authoritative: TARGET_REPOSITORY_SOURCE != AUTHORITY TO PERFORM PRIVILEGED DELIVERY MUTATIONS.

Grant capabilities least-privilege, only when the repository participates in the accepted normal delivery model, trust/storage requirements can be satisfied, and no narrower mechanism covers the contract. No repository receives a capability for symmetry. Each independently meaningful repository/capability change has its own Leaf and exactly one Primary Delivery PR. Consume existing owners without replacing or reparenting them.

## Authenticated baseline and capability decision

Protected `SecPal/.github/main` at `71daad75d90ab2ce07be3a8d00ff1192d08a2c11` matches current canonical contracts, registry/schema and executor bytes; GitHub verifies its signature. Authenticated active identities: .github, frontend, api, contracts, android, secpal.app and deployment are public, non-archived repositories with protected main; operations is private and information-only. GuardGuide and guardguide.de are excluded as retired/deleted.

The normal reusable model comprises three independently selected capabilities:

- `lifecycle_authority_policy`: schema 1.0, existing SSH-only keys/roles and repository-local append-only publication journal. Reuse accepted Contracts/deployment/secpal.app policy; bind the exact repository URL, lifecycle ref and real ruleset ID. No historical repairs/admissions or initializations are copied.
- `pre_enrollment_integration_policy`: the accepted closed schema-1.0 `integrate-pre-enrollment-draft` / `PRE_ENROLLMENT_DRAFT_INTEGRATION` policy. It authenticates lifecycle absence using maintained lifecycle policy; no target product infrastructure is needed beyond that lifecycle registration/protection.
- `enrolled_draft_integration_policy`: accepted #1065 / PR #1068 supplies the otherwise missing initial native enrolled Draft current-main path. PRE_ENROLLMENT rejects CURRENT/genesis and Ready integration rejects Draft. The current schema and executor select this closed policy by exact repository, with no repository-specific behavior, special signer, or deployment infrastructure requirement. The documented .github/deployment pair describes existing registration scope; it does not define a permanent architecture restriction. Roll out the existing capability to the other five appropriate public delivery repositories.

Both integration policies permit NON_FORCE_PUSH_EXACT_PR_BRANCH, one candidate, one push, force_push=false, automatic_retry=false and merge_pull_request=false. Generic BRANCH_WRITE, wildcard repositories, arbitrary refs/main writes, replacement PRs, retry loops and automatic merge remain prohibited.

Typed Ready integration consumes exact registry signature/validation projection and maintained lifecycle CURRENT; there is no `ready_integration_policy`. Hermetic repository-shaped authority tests and read-only registry/executor projection must prove selection for every lifecycle-enabled public target without any fake Ready mutation.

## Existing owners and intentional exceptions

- .github and deployment are complete positive references; create no symmetry Leaf.
- Preserve Contracts lifecycle/ruleset owners #964/#969 and #967/#968; #1038 owns a particular historical Ready adoption, not generic capability registration.
- Preserve secpal.app lifecycle/adoption #1037/#1039 and #1074/#1075, and pre-enrollment #1080/#1081; create only its missing enrolled-Draft Leaf. Completed downstream #332/#333 and #352/#353 are outside this effort.
- Consume #705 / PR #706 and #1061 for Operations. #1061 already owns the accepted central protected .github journal exception, which current main cannot yet represent. Do not duplicate or absorb it. Current private information-only Operations is outside the public protected-main product-delivery integration baseline. No extra integration grant, plan upgrade, visibility change or unavailable private protection is appropriate to this role. Future applicability follows accepted #1061 and an independently justified role change.
- Frontend #1809 / PR #1810 remains an open historical Draft. Its terminal prerequisite is the Frontend pre-enrollment capability Leaf, which itself consumes lifecycle authority. Add that native dependency; do not mutate or resume #1810.

## Child work plan

Native sub-issue order expresses Frontend first, then API, Contracts, secpal.app and Android. One Leaf per missing capability: Frontend lifecycle/pre-enrollment/enrolled-Draft; API lifecycle/pre-enrollment/enrolled-Draft; Contracts pre-enrollment/enrolled-Draft; secpal.app enrolled-Draft; Android lifecycle/pre-enrollment/enrolled-Draft. Integration Leaves for newly lifecycle-enabled repositories depend natively on their lifecycle Leaf because absence/CURRENT and journal claims require its accepted policy. No taste-based dependency serializes independent capabilities.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every required capability Leaf completes its normal finite signed Draft -> PRE_READY -> one Draft-to-Ready -> Review 1/1 -> bounded remediation/integration -> merge lifecycle and is closed/completed.
- Accepted-main read-back after each merge proves exact capability admission, unchanged unrelated entries/existing policies, actual target storage/protection, read-only maintained selection, and removal of the prior missing-policy rejection.
- An authenticated final matrix covers all eight active repositories: lifecycle authority, storage model/ref, protection/ruleset, both Draft policies, Ready selectability, standard signer policy, intentional exceptions, owners/references and executor/projection result.
- No active public delivery repository lacks a normal capability required by the accepted finite model; every omission has authenticated least-privilege justification and Operations ownership remains intact.
- Minimum Frontend chain completion structurally unblocks #1809 without executing #1810.
- No live api.secpal.dev/app.secpal.dev dependency, target product/source/environment mutation, duplicate work, Android resumption or deferred Node-26 delivery occurs.
- Canonical Epic closure maps each criterion to exact completed child Leaves/PRs and authenticated matrix evidence before explicit completed closure. No implementation PR closes this Epic.

## Non-goals

No product delivery, README/API documentation implementation, Contracts Node migration, Android feature/source/signing/release changes, secpal.app documentation, deployment features, new lifecycle concept, signer, trust root, generic branch-write authority or fake initial publication. Target administrative mutation is limited to the exact missing lifecycle ruleset and read-back; the branch may remain absent until first authenticated publication.

## Evidence plan

Retain fresh main/identity/ruleset/duplicate observations and policy reproductions. Every Leaf uses fail-first positive/negative registry and maintained projection/executor tests, wrong-repository and malformed/widened-policy rejection before mutation, relevant focused validation, changed-file pre-commit, formatting/Markdown if touched, REUSE/SPDX, static policy, diff/preflight checks, one final frozen-tree Complete Registered Validation epoch with receipt/final attestation, hosted gates and finite review. Reuse existing generic invariant coverage and perform no downstream mutation. Workspace evidence is temporary and non-authoritative; native graph links/state remain authoritative.

## Final authenticated capability checkpoint

This is an incomplete completion checkpoint, not Epic closure. Protected SecPal/.github/main at 30077f41a485d25c13a825331d86d6a1f49e4710 is GitHub-signature verified. All eight active repository identities and existing capability values were authenticated; the eleven new accepted capabilities are the only capability additions. The existing repository set and all pre-existing capability values remain unchanged.

### Independent Leaf outcomes

| Contract | Native Leaf | Primary PR | Accepted outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Frontend lifecycle | #1084 | #1096 | Merged; CLOSED / completed; post-merge accepted |
| Frontend pre-enrollment | #1085 | #1100 | Ready; blocked by existing #1031 / PR #1035 |
| Frontend enrolled-Draft | #1086 | #1101 | Merged; CLOSED / completed; post-merge accepted |
| API lifecycle | #1087 | #1102 | Merged; CLOSED / completed; post-merge accepted |
| API pre-enrollment | #1088 | #1103 | Merged; CLOSED / completed; post-merge accepted |
| API enrolled-Draft | #1089 | #1104 | Merged; CLOSED / completed; post-merge accepted |
| Contracts pre-enrollment | #1090 | #1105 | Merged; CLOSED / completed; post-merge accepted |
| Contracts enrolled-Draft | #1091 | #1106 | Merged; CLOSED / completed; post-merge accepted |
| secpal.app enrolled-Draft | #1092 | #1107 | Merged; CLOSED / completed; post-merge accepted |
| Android lifecycle | #1093 | #1108 | Merged; CLOSED / completed; post-merge accepted |
| Android pre-enrollment | #1094 | #1109 | Merged; CLOSED / completed; post-merge accepted |

### Capability matrix

issue.body:
## Goal

Define and implement one maintained, fail-closed contract for truthful terminal disposition and narrowly authorized successor handling of the never-enrolled, directly-Ready `SecPal/.github` PR #706 belonging to Issue #705.

Prefer a finite, auditable retirement and non-resetting successor disposition over adding a permanent historical-Ready exception. Establish whether exactly one genuinely Draft successor under the same #705 contract can lawfully complete delivery. Do not preauthorize that successor or any review.

## Exact historical case

Fresh authenticated protected `.github/main`: `eab46aa7a3d828e0f1b2e75a48a8ff8f135dec93` (GitHub verified).

- Delivery owner: [#705](https://github.com/SecPal/.github/issues/705), OPEN; existing sole primary [PR #706](https://github.com/SecPal/.github/pull/706), OPEN, non-Draft, unmerged and conflicting.
- Original PR creation: `2026-08-22T21:53:28Z`, directly Ready. Complete native timeline has zero `ReadyForReviewEvent` and zero `ConvertToDraftEvent` observations. Its direct-Ready creation is invalid under canonical Draft-first governance; historical recognition must not represent it as compliant or invent an earlier Draft lifecycle.
- Source head: `4760603b6f23bbd652432e82d1c6dc193c93c467`; tree: `c4c750238cfc4338d20d240f9bfec6e481ac5587`; sole parent: `d56bd229c11848ac9231023cd49f1e968486c94e`. GitHub verifies the source signature; independent accepted-main SSH-key verification also passed.
- Existing provider review objects: Copilot `PRR_kwDOQFR1MM8AAAABKhc_ug` and Codex Code `PRR_kwDOQFR1MM8AAAABKhdOcQ`, both on that source head. Two unresolved, non-outdated threads remain: `PRRT_kwDOQFR1MM6bbkqN` and `PRRT_kwDOQFR1MM6bbkqP`.
- Attempted Security acquisition reported a usage-limit failure in comment `IC_kwDOQFR1MM8AAAABQNbsGQ`. No successful Security completion was authenticated. Two provider objects are observations, not proof of two workflow cycles or a zero consumed budget.
- Protected lifecycle journal tip: `135aeb76d9476526a27b57bdb79c764b8ba18824`. Maintained verification authenticated 588 publication entries and no #705 CURRENT, native admission or recovery; fresh protection and tip read-back preserved that absence conclusion. Missing CURRENT is not permission to initialize a fresh lifecycle. No receipt trailer exists on the source, but this does not prove a historical validation receipt was never issued.

## Prerequisite necessity and ownership

Completed independent qualifications established `HISTORICAL_LIFECYCLE_INCOMPATIBLE` and `NO_LAWFUL_PATH_YET`: ordinary native admission, Exact-State-Adoption versions 1–4, legacy checkpoint, `PR_REBOUND` and maintained recovery paths cannot presently admit this truthful chronology. Closing #706 would release its open claim but would not establish a lawful successor or replenish review entitlement. A conservative Draft baseline carrying Review 1 cannot pass first Ready through budget admission alone; the maintained exception requires an actual authenticated historical Draft review, which must not be fabricated.

Authenticated searches of open and completed governance contracts, plus the complete native open-issue inventory, found no owner of this exact missing capability. Consume completed #692/#750/#752, #798/#834/#845 and the maintained signing/publication primitives. Preserve separate #1014 Draft-bootstrap composition, #1061 Operations lifecycle enrollment, #1083 capability onboarding, #1155 already-enrolled review-publication reconciliation, and exact Governance-Amendment registrations for #960/PR #961 and #1053/PR #1055. None grants authority for #705/PR #706. Historical duplicate #707 does not own this recovery capability.

This is independently meaningful central governance work, outside #705's bounded Operations audit-registration implementation. #705 must remain natively blocked by this Leaf; #676 must retain its native prerequisite #705. Native relationships, not this prose, govern execution.

## Acceptance criteria

- Independently authenticate the exact repository, #705, PR #706, head/tree/ordered parent, signature, complete creation/review chronology, current graph and protected-journal absence. Bind actual fresh observations and accepted-main tooling; reject identity/source drift, competing enrollment and candidate-local authority.
- Preserve the directly-Ready historical creation and its Draft-first violation, both provider review objects, both unresolved threads, attempted Security acquisition and complete historical source evidence. Record zero actual Draft-to-Ready transitions; never invent a Draft origin, review, successful Security verdict, receipt, attestation or publication.
- Define and implement a terminal, auditable unmerged retirement procedure which preserves all historical evidence, performs no thread-resolution or history rewrite, and releases only the original open primary claim. Authenticate the exact preconditions and independently read back the persisted result; ambiguous or partial mutation permits bounded observation/reconciliation only, not blind retry or further improvised writes.
- Establish whether a single new genuinely Draft primary successor can be authorized under the same unchanged #705 contract. Define and enforce the exact permitted order of retirement, successor creation and lifecycle admission/enrollment. If required evidence or a lawful sequence is unavailable, report that precise blocker and authorize no successor.
- Require independently authenticated review-accounting disposition and separate explicit, exact human authorization before any successor can request or trigger another assessment. Distinguish provider objects from canonical workflow consumption, preserve prior assessment/findings and failed Security acquisition, and bind their truthful disposition to the successor decision. Missing publication or a new PR number never establishes zero consumption or a new entitlement.
- Forbid counter resets, treating the previous assessment as nonexistent, fabricated historical events, automatic Ready/Draft toggles, recursive review, replacement chains and an unbounded series of successors. Permit at most one exact successor, with one-use/replay protection through existing authenticated authority where possible. A further failure stops at a separate explicit decision boundary.
- Keep the canonical Draft-first rule intact for every normal delivery. Require successful exact-source Code/Security admission and all mandatory lifecycle/evidence gates through their accepted authority; source correctness or green CI alone cannot advance the delivery. No historical observation is silently reclassified as authorization.
- Preserve the existing protected lifecycle journal, signing roles, signer keys, trust boundaries, strict required checks and branch/ruleset settings. Introduce no journal, signer, trust root, generic branch-write or arbitrary-delivery exception. Do not borrow another delivery's Governance-Amendment registration.
- Apply `SIMPLIFY_BEFORE_EXTEND`: inventory and reuse maintained disposition, admission, publication, authorization and finite-state primitives. Introduce only the minimum demonstrably necessary, exact-case authority, with an explicit permanent-complexity assessment. If broader architectural change is necessary, report a genuine design blocker rather than widening this Leaf automatically.
- Add maintained positive and adversarial tests before executable changes. Cover truthful original chronology, bounded terminal retirement, authorized successor eligibility or fail-closed ineligibility, complete review-accounting and Security failure preservation, wrong repository/issue/PR/head/tree/parent, forged/missing authority, hidden history or receipt substitution, stale/raced enrollment, replay, partial writes, multiple successors, counter reset, fabricated Draft/Ready events, unsupported review acquisition and normal Draft-first regressions.
- Deliver one primary implementation PR for this Leaf through the normal signed Draft-first finite lifecycle, proportionate focused tests, complete registered validation, required evidence, independent review and normal acceptance. This Leaf does not reopen completed governance work or consume #705's delivery/review budget.
- Accept the recovery contract and implementation on protected main before applying any part to #705/PR #706. Independent accepted-main read-back must requalify the exact historical case without mutation and identify the verified next operation and its still-required operator authority. Candidate tests, Issue creation, this prerequisite relationship and Leaf completion do not themselves authorize consumption. If qualification fails, retain this Leaf open with the exact blocker.

## Ownership, hierarchy and exclusions

Native parent is the existing #1032 lifecycle-governance continuation Sub-Epic under #664. #667 already has 100 direct children; #1032 had 38 at qualification and explicitly owns new in-family corrective Leaves. Preserve all existing parents, sibling order and unrelated dependencies; no new Epic or Sub-Epic is needed. #705 remains its existing standalone delivery owner.

No Operations Controller implementation or installation, Operations registration source patch, infrastructure/provider/host operation, Polyscope maintenance, application deployment, reference-server access, GuardGuide reenrollment, required-check mutation, automatic Issue/PR closure, new #705 primary PR, replacement branch, review acquisition, Draft/Ready change or lifecycle publication is authorized by creation of this Leaf. Those exact target operations remain prohibited until accepted maintained authority and separate explicit consumption authorization exist.
